You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Each 10x10 input contains four disconnected colored objects: two objects in each of two colors. Output removes them from original positions, preserves each object's shape/color exactly, and relocates them into two lower-half columns: objects of the color at top-left go to the left column; objects of the color at top-right go to the right column. The bottom-left and bottom-right objects join the column of their own color. Sample examples show varying vertical placement within the lower half; do not assume fixed shifts. In this solved test, input colors/objects: color 2 top-left (bbox rows1-3 cols0-3; shape [[2,2,2,2],[0,0,0,2],[0,0,2,2]]) and bottom-right 2x3 block; color 3 top-right 1x3 line and bottom-left shape (bbox rows5-7 cols1-4: [[0,0,3,3],[3,3,3,3],[0,0,3,0]]). Correct output places the 2x3 block at rows4-5 cols0-2; the 2 top-left object at rows7-9 cols0-3; 3 line at row5 cols5-7; and the bottom-left 3 shape at rows7-9 cols5-8, preserving local shapes. Submitted output accepted first try, no wrong attempts, after four demos.
Demos showing shape-preserving translation and color-column grouping:
1) Colors 1 (top-left & lower-left) and 6 (top-right & middle-left): output all objects in lower half; color6 objects at left, color1 at right. Some test demo object seemed to lose cells, but later demos indicate preserve shape; avoid relying on unclear transcription.

3) Colors 8/4: color8 objects at left, color4 at right; translated objects retain shapes, generally into lower half. 
4) Colors 7/9: color7 objects at left, color9 at right. Specifically color7 top-left object goes to rows7-9 cols0-3, bottom-right block goes rows4-5 cols0-2; color9 top-right 2x3 goes rows6-7 cols5-7 and bottom-left 5-cell line goes row9 cols5-9. Thus column assignment follows the colors of the two top objects (top-left color = left column; top-right color = right column), not numeric color ordering. Output horizontal anchors can vary modestly, but the examples use approximately c0 and c5. Preserve grid dimensions and background zeros.'''); entry
